title: mini-attestation-manifest-and-retrofit-guide
content:
Purpose:
A compact "mini" attestation manifest that teams can retrofit into existing customer-managed networking installs with minimal infra changes. Focus: provide an evidence bundle that is small, verifiable, and friendly to low-bandwidth customer edges (satellite, on-prem with strict egress). This doc is an actionable PRD + retrofit guide for product + solutions + SRE to validate and pilot with 2–3 customers.

Background / problem we keep seeing:
- Customers want a way to show changes to their VPC/network configuration were approved and observable by their operators and by Redwood.
- Full attestation/evidence bundles are heavy (certs, long logs) and increase storage/query costs; customers on constrained links complain about onboarding friction.
- We need a pragmatic intermediate format that satisfies auditors for most customers while enabling fast rollouts and cheap retention.

Goals (measurable):
- Draft a minimal JSON manifest format (< 4KB typical) that can be produced by operator CLI or our agent-side small binary.
- Integrate manifest emission as an optional step in the existing approval gate flow (can be on by default for new private installs, opt-in for legacy).
- Support cryptographic signature (customer HSM/KMS or Redwood signing key) and a compact proof-of-origin (hash + short sig).
- Provide retention tiers: 7d (ephemeral), 90d (audit-lite), 365d (customer request) with cost estimates.
- Reduce average onboarding payload by >70% vs full evidence bundles.

Constraints / non-goals:
- This is not a full legal attestation standard for high-regulated customers (FedRAMP/IL4). It is intended for enterprise and mid-market customers who need tamper-evident traces and low-bandwidth export.
- We will not implement a new global PKI; we will integrate with existing KMS/HSM options and support signed manifests via customer-provided keys where available.

Design sketch: manifest fields (informal)
- manifest_version: v1
- id: short-uuid (base62)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- change_summary: short human text (<= 240 chars)
- change_type: enum (firewall-rule, route, peering, nat, operator-note)
- actor: { name_or_service, id_hint }  -- note: keep concise (string like "operator:alice@acme")
- approval_pointers: list of approval IDs (could be Redwood approval-id or external ticket id like JIRA PD-####)
- evidence_digest: sha256 hex of the full evidence archive (if available)
- signatures: list of short sig descriptors (sig_scheme:key_id:base64sig)
- retention_tier: short-tag (ephemeral/standard/long)
- small_metadata: key=value; comma-separated pairs (max 256 chars)
- optional: k-v of customer_correlation_id, cluster, region

Notes on format:
- Keep each manifest line under 4KB and whole doc generally < 4KB. If a full log exists, store it in the evidence archive (S3/zip) and reference via evidence_digest and an optional storage URL that is ephemeral/signed for retrieval.
- Signatures: allow two forms: Redwood-signed (for cases where customer cannot sign) or customer-signed (preferred). Support signature verification via KMS public keys exposed by customer or via Redwood admin-managed key escrow (only when customer consents).

Integration points with current approval gates:
- Emit manifest on approval completion (synchronous step).
- Route manifest to three places: (1) customer sidecar (optional), (2) Redwood compact-index (searchable metadata + digests), (3) optional external webhook (SIEM).
- Approval gate UI: add a "generate compact attestation" checkbox and default retention tier selector.

Sampling and telemetry:
- Default: emit manifest for 100% of approval events during pilot for visibility. After pilot, default to 10% sample for high-frequency customers, with on-demand full capture via toggle in Console.
- Telemetry to capture: bytes emitted per manifest, verification success/failure rates, signature latency, per-customer retention cost estimate.

Storage, query, and cost model (back-of-envelope):
- Average manifest stored as compact-index row (200–800 bytes) + optional evidence archive for ~10% of changes.
- Cost estimates (rough): compact-index storage $0.00002 / manifest / month; evidence archive avg 50KB for 10% events -> S3-equivalent $0.00012 / event / month. These are placeholders; infra should produce monthly estimates for each customer during onboarding.

Operator UX + Retrofit steps (how to add to existing installs):
1) Minimal install: drop a lightweight binary (attest-agent) or enable an agent in the operator container. The agent listens to approval outputs and emits manifest JSON to a local buffer.
2) Signing: if customer has KMS, agent calls KMS.sign(manifest_digest) and stores signature locally; otherwise agent POSTs manifest to Redwood signing endpoint (with envelope token).
3) Delivery: agent pushes manifest to customer-side store (NFS/S3) or to Redwood via encrypted channel. When bandwidth is constrained, agent batches and transmits during maintenance windows.
4) Console: show compact attestation in the approval timeline with verification status. Provide a "download full evidence" link that requests the full archive if present.

Pilot plan (90 days):
- Week 0–2: prototype manifest schema + agent PoC. Integrate with approval gate demo flow.
- Week 3–6: internal SRE + solutions testing on two internal clusters; produce cost telemetry.
- Week 7–14: select 2 pilot customers (one low-bandwidth telco, one enterprise) for retrofit; enable 100% manifests.
- Week 15–20: analyze telemetry, adjust sampling defaults, finalize retention UI.

Acceptance criteria for Beta:
- Manifest verification succeeds end-to-end for >98% of pilot events.
- Average manifest size < 3.5KB and median < 1.2KB.
- No onboarding blockers reported by pilot customers; delivery time for manifests under 15s for synchronous signing flows.

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODOs):
- Should the manifest be canonical JSON (sorted keys) to simplify signature verification? Pros: deterministic sigs; Cons: operator libs need to implement canonicalization.
- How to handle revocation/rotation of signing keys without making past manifests unverifiable? Proposal: include key_id + key_rotation_epoch in manifest and maintain a rotation ledger. Need legal review on chain-of-trust implications.
- Retention policy enforcement for customer-managed archives: if a customer deletes their archive, our evidence_digest still references nothing — should we store an immutable short proof (hash only) inside Redwood even for ephemeral-retention? Privacy and cost implications.
- Edge case: concurrent approvals that touch same resource produce multiple manifests — should we produce a merged manifest? probably not; produce independent manifests and let a higher-level replayer synthesize.

Testing & QA ideas:
- Fuzz manifest generator to ensure max size constraints hold with unusually long metadata fields.
- Verification harness: a tiny library that validates signature formats across KMS providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) and Redwood signing.
- Recovery test: simulate customer archive deletion and validate that compact-index plus evidence_digest suffice for basic forensic queries.

Next steps (owners & quick tasks):
- Product: finalize manifest schema draft for review (owner: Ava) — due 2024-10-09.
- Eng (applied-ml infra): PoC of attest-agent that can sign via AWS KMS and batch uploads (owner: Diego) — due 2024-10-23.
- SRE: add compact-index table prototype and cost telemetry pipeline (owner: Priya) — due 2024-11-01.
- Solutions: recruit pilot customers and prepare onboarding checklist (owner: Liam) — ongoing.

Notes to self / rough TODO list:
- Add sample manifests (3 examples: firewall-rule allow, route-add, operator-note).
- Write a small FAQ for legal/infosec covering key rotation and subpoena scenarios.
- Link to Console mockups for "compact attestation" in the approval timeline (Confluence link above).

- Jira: PD-2147 (mini-attestation pilot)
- GH: private-attestation-proto/README has initial schema examples

Unresolved: decision on default sampling after pilot (100% vs 10% for high-frequency). Put on next PD sync agenda.

End of draft.
